positioning: The aqua-eyed mix of Siamese and Burmese. A plush, playful cat with a mink coat.
story: The Tonkinese is the middle road between the Siamese and the Burmese. Cats that looked like this have been recorded in Asia for centuries, and a brown cat called Wong Mau, brought to California in the 1930s, is often named as the ancestor. Breeders in Canada and the United States then built the breed in the 1960s by crossing Siamese and Burmese.

The coat comes in a pattern called mink, which is in between a Siamese point and a Burmese solid. The body is a soft, warm shade, and the face, ears, legs and tail are a deeper tone, with a gentle blend between them. Colors include natural, champagne, blue and platinum.

The eyes are the star. A Tonkinese has aquamarine eyes, a blue-green shade unique to the breed, set in a rounded wedge face with medium ears. The body is medium and muscular, a little heavier than it looks, and the coat is short, silky and dense.

The personality takes the best of both parents. Tonkinese are outgoing, playful and affectionate, with the Siamese love of conversation softened by a gentler voice. They are leaping, climbing athletes, and they want to be at the center of every household activity.

These cats love company. A Tonkinese does not like to be alone, and it does best with people at home or with a feline friend. Many learn tricks, fetch and walk on a leash. They get on well with children and with dogs, and they like a warm lap in the evening.

The coat is easy, a weekly comb is plenty. Health notes include dental disease, a respiratory tendency and, in some lines, a condition called amyloidosis, so ask breeders about screening. A healthy Tonkinese can live well into its teens. Provide height, toys and affection.
fblocks: From Tonkin, an old name for northern Vietnam, though the breed was built in North America.
A pattern in between the Siamese point and the Burmese solid.
Outgoing, playful and sociable. It needs company and does not like to be alone.
A short, silky coat in natural, champagne, blue or platinum, with aqua eyes.
Built in the 1960s from Siamese and Burmese crosses.
Offer height, games and company. A Tonkinese wants to be part of everything.
Ask about dental and breathing health. Comb weekly.
days: The Tonkinese has aqua eyes, a blue-green shade found only in this breed.
A brown cat named Wong Mau is often named as the mother of the Tonkinese.
A coat in between two coats, and a voice in between two voices.
It appears at every conversation and takes a side.
The middle way is often the warmest.
Ask whether it is a Siamese or a Burmese, and watch it ignore you.
A silky head under your hand, and a purr that turns the lights low.
last_walk:
Soft peach light on the patio, and the summer night is coming.
The Tonkinese has chatted, climbed and followed every footstep this week. Now it sits on the low wall, aqua eyes bright, and watches the sky go pink. One more look at the garden, then a lap.
